  1. AI is killing All About Berlin

    • AI
    • Economics
    • Search Engines

    806 points · 710 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 06:47 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The author wrote that AI-driven answer products and search changes were reducing traffic to All About Berlin, threatening the economics of a locally focused information site. The essay described the concern as both a business and web-ecosystem problem.

    Discussion — Commenters debated uncompensated training and answer extraction, creator displacement, concentration of power, and the long-run supply of useful web content. Suggested responses included revenue sharing, regulation, subscriptions, local or open models, and business-model changes.

  2. Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%

    • AI
    • Economics
    • Search Engines

    709 points · 563 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 00:17 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — RevScope argues that Google AI Overviews reduce outbound clicks, citing a randomized desktop-Chrome experiment in which visible Overviews averaged fewer external clicks and estimating an overall organic-click loss. The article combines that working paper with observational Pew and DataForSEO material, states limitations in the modeling and sampling, and finds little demonstrated value in GEO tactics beyond conventional SEO and reputable third-party presence.

    Discussion — The thread debated whether AI answers undermine publishers, hobby communities, and other sources that fund public information, or mainly displace low-value SEO and ad-heavy content. Commenters also discussed copyright, citations, paywalls, revenue sharing, Google’s earlier incentives, and whether search should prioritize direct primary sources; the author acknowledged possible commercial-query bias in one dataset.

    Week of 2026-11-20

    • Search Engines

    47 points · 30 comments · 13 Nov 2026, 23:26 (Europe/London) · HN discussion
